nodes.title: Architecture Layer
nodes.definition: A level of abstraction in the architecture stack (business, conceptual, semantic, information, logical, physical, technical) with its own questions, artifacts and decision rights.

nodes.title: Architecture Decision Management Capability
nodes.summary: The ability to take, record, govern and trace architecture decisions consistently across teams.

nodes.title: Historical Data Reconstruction Capability
nodes.summary: The ability of an organisation to reconstruct past states of its data - as they were true and as they were known - for operations, audit and regulation.

nodes.title: Architecture Decision
nodes.definition: A justified choice between alternatives that affects the structure, qualities or constraints of an architecture, recorded independently of the architecture documentation it shapes.

nodes.title: Data Architecture
nodes.definition: The discipline and resulting structures that define how an organisation's data is described, organised, integrated, governed and realized across systems, from business meaning to technical implementation.

nodes.title: Information Architecture
nodes.definition: The structuring of information — its meaning, organisation, classification and relationships — so that people and processes can find, understand and use it consistently.

nodes.title: Layered Model Derivation
nodes.summary: Derive models layer by layer - governed concepts, then information model, then logical, then physical - keeping a traceability link at every step.

nodes.title: Decisions Belong to Their Layer
nodes.summary: Each architecture decision is taken at the layer where it belongs, by the role with decision rights for that layer, and lower layers do not silently override higher-layer decisions.

nodes.title: Each Data Element Has an Authoritative Source
nodes.summary: For every shared data element, exactly one authoritative source is designated; other copies are derived and traceable to it.
nodes.path: 02-architecture/principles/Each Data Element Has an Authoritative Source.md

nodes.title: Technology-Neutral Architecture First
nodes.summary: Architecture is expressed in technology-neutral concepts and patterns first; technology-specific choices reference and realize them.

nodes.title: Data Model
nodes.definition: A structured representation of data — its entities, attributes, relationships and constraints — at a stated level of abstraction and for a stated purpose.

nodes.title: Information Model
nodes.definition: A paradigm-independent model that represents governed meaning as information structures — classes, attributes, relationships, cardinalities and information-level constraints including history requirements.

nodes.title: Temporal Data Management
nodes.definition: The capture, storage and querying of how data and knowledge about data change over time, including valid time (when a fact is true in reality) and transaction time (when the fact was recorded).

nodes.title: Conceptual Data Model
nodes.definition: A data model that identifies the business things of interest and their high-level relationships, without attributes' technical detail and independent of any implementation.

nodes.title: Logical Data Model
nodes.definition: A data model that structures information in a chosen data paradigm (e.g. relational, dimensional, graph, document) with keys, relationships and constraints, independent of a specific product.

nodes.title: Physical Data Model
nodes.definition: A data model that specifies how a logical data model is realized in a specific data store, including data types, storage structures, indexing, partitioning and physical history mechanisms.

nodes.title: Meaning Before Representation
nodes.summary: The meaning of a concept is defined and governed before, and independently of, its representation in information and data models.

nodes.title: Business Concept
nodes.definition: A unit of business meaning — a thing, event, role or idea the organisation talks and decides about — identified by a preferred term and a governed definition.

nodes.title: Controlled Vocabulary
nodes.definition: A governed list of approved terms, each with a defined meaning, used to label and classify information consistently.

nodes.title: Ontology
nodes.definition: A formal, explicit specification of concepts in a domain, their properties and relationships, and logical axioms, expressed so that machines can reason over it.

nodes.title: Semantic Model
nodes.definition: An explicit, governed representation of meaning — concepts, their definitions, identity criteria and semantic relationships such as specialization, generalization, part-whole and equivalence.

nodes.title: Taxonomy
nodes.definition: A hierarchical classification of concepts organised by broader/narrower relationships.

nodes.title: Metadata Is Captured by Design
nodes.summary: Metadata is produced as part of designing and delivering data assets, preferably automatically, rather than documented afterwards.

nodes.title: Data Lineage
nodes.definition: Metadata describing the origin of data and the path, transformations and dependencies through which it flows from source to consumption.

nodes.title: Metadata
nodes.definition: Data that describes other data or data-related assets — their meaning, structure, origin, quality, ownership, usage, security and processing.

nodes.title: Data Governance
nodes.definition: The exercise of authority, control and shared decision-making over the management of data assets — who may decide what about data, on which basis, and how compliance is ensured.

nodes.title: Data Ownership
nodes.definition: The assignment of accountability for a defined set of data — its meaning, quality, access and lifecycle — to a business role with the authority to make decisions about it.

nodes.title: Data Stewardship
nodes.definition: The operational care for data on behalf of its owner — maintaining definitions, metadata, quality rules and issue resolution.

nodes.title: Data Has an Accountable Owner
nodes.summary: Every governed data set, concept and architecture artifact has exactly one accountable owner with decision rights over it.

nodes.title: Architecture Board
nodes.summary: Governance body that approves architecture decisions above the agreed threshold and decides on exceptions and cross-domain conflicts.

nodes.title: Data Architect
nodes.summary: Architect responsible for the realization of information in data structures, flows, history mechanisms and authoritative sources.

nodes.title: Data Custodian
nodes.summary: Technical role operating the storage, security and availability of data according to owner decisions.

nodes.title: Data Owner
nodes.summary: Business role accountable for a defined set of data: its meaning, quality requirements, access and lifecycle.

nodes.title: Data Steward
nodes.summary: Operational role caring for data on behalf of the owner: definitions, metadata, quality rules and issue resolution.

nodes.title: Domain Architect
nodes.summary: Architect accountable for coherent architecture within one business domain, aligned with enterprise principles.

nodes.title: Domain Expert
nodes.summary: Subject-matter authority whose knowledge of the business domain informs definitions and models.

nodes.title: Enterprise Architect
nodes.summary: Architect accountable for enterprise-wide principles, standards and cross-domain coherence.

nodes.title: Information Architect
nodes.summary: Architect responsible for information models that represent governed meaning as paradigm-independent structures.

nodes.title: Ontology Engineer
nodes.summary: Specialist who formalises semantic models as ontologies and ensures their logical consistency.

nodes.title: Platform Architect
nodes.summary: Architect responsible for data platform capabilities, technical standards and technology lifecycle.

nodes.title: Privacy Specialist
nodes.summary: Specialist who assesses personal data processing for privacy compliance and advises on privacy by design.

nodes.title: Security Architect
nodes.summary: Architect responsible for security architecture, classification schemes and security controls for data.

nodes.title: Semantic Architect
nodes.summary: Architect responsible for the structure, formalism and integrity of semantic models across domains.

nodes.title: Solution Architect
nodes.summary: Architect responsible for the design of a specific solution within enterprise and data architecture constraints.

nodes.title: Data Quality
nodes.definition: The degree to which data is fit for its intended uses, assessed against explicit requirements along defined quality dimensions.

nodes.title: Quality Is Managed at the Source
nodes.summary: Data quality issues are prevented and corrected as close as possible to where data is created, rather than repaired downstream.

nodes.title: Data Quality Dimension
nodes.definition: A named aspect of data quality — such as completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, validity or uniqueness — along which quality requirements are specified and measured.

nodes.title: Data Platform
nodes.definition: The integrated set of technical capabilities — storage, processing, integration, metadata, security and operations — on which data is stored, transformed and served.

nodes.title: Data Integration
nodes.definition: The combination of data from different sources, and its movement between systems, so that it can be used consistently for a shared purpose.

nodes.title: Data Lifecycle
nodes.definition: The sequence of stages data passes through — creation or acquisition, storage, use, change, sharing, archiving and disposal — together with the rules governing each transition.

nodes.title: Historical Requirements Are Explicit
nodes.summary: Requirements for history — which data, which time dimensions, which reconstruction questions and retention — are stated explicitly at the information layer before a history mechanism is chosen.

nodes.title: Data Migration
nodes.definition: The controlled, one-time or phased transfer of data from source systems to target systems, including mapping, transformation, cleansing, validation and reconciliation, with preserved meaning and traceability.

nodes.title: Golden Record
nodes.definition: The consolidated, best-known version of a master data entity, assembled from one or more source records according to survivorship rules.

nodes.title: Master Data
nodes.definition: The data about core business entities — such as parties, products, locations and assets — that is shared across processes and systems and provides context to transactions.

nodes.title: Reference Data
nodes.definition: Sets of permissible values — codes and their meanings — used to classify or categorise other data, often defined by external bodies and shared across systems.

nodes.title: Architecture Governance Model
nodes.summary: The overall model of how data and architecture decisions are governed — layered decision rights, roles, lifecycle, controls and change process — treated as a first-class architectural layer.

nodes.title: Governance Lifecycle
nodes.summary: The lifecycle states of governed artifacts and knowledge objects, the allowed and invalid transitions, and who may perform each transition.

nodes.title: Governance Roles
nodes.summary: Overview of the reusable governance roles, their layer focus and their decision rights, linking to the individual role definitions.

nodes.title: Knowledge Quality Model
nodes.summary: Quality criteria and quality statuses for knowledge objects, and how quality relates to lifecycle status, confidence and epistemic status.

nodes.title: Knowledge Repository Governance
nodes.summary: How this knowledge base itself is governed — repository roles, Git workflow, automated validation, human-in-the-loop approval and rules for LLM contributions.

nodes.title: Terminology Governance
nodes.summary: How preferred terms, definitions, synonyms, forbidden terms and abbreviations are governed and how terminology inconsistencies are detected.

nodes.title: Knowledge Change Review Process
nodes.summary: The pull-request based process by which a proposed change to the knowledge graph is validated, reviewed, decided per governance level, recorded, merged and published.

nodes.title: Separate Decision per Governance Level
nodes.summary: An approval contains one decision for each governance level the object's layers require - semantic, information model, data architecture, technical - never a single combined approval.

nodes.title: Separation of Duties in Approval
nodes.summary: Nobody approves a change they proposed or an object they own.

nodes.title: Status Change Requires Governance Record
nodes.summary: An object may only be approved, published, implemented, deprecated or retired when an append-only governance record establishes that transition for its current version.

nodes.title: Architecture Decisions Are Traceable
nodes.summary: Significant architecture decisions are recorded with their context, options and rationale, and are traceable from source knowledge to implementation.

nodes.title: Governance Is Embedded in Delivery
nodes.summary: Governance controls are built into the delivery workflow as automated and review steps, rather than applied as a separate documentation phase at the end.

nodes.title: Apache Iceberg
nodes.summary: Open table format for large analytic datasets providing snapshots, time travel, schema evolution and hidden partitioning on file/object storage.

nodes.title: SQL Server Temporal Tables
nodes.summary: Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL feature that implements system-versioned (transaction-time) tables with automatic history tables and FOR SYSTEM_TIME queries.

nodes.title: Debezium
nodes.summary: Open-source, log-based change data capture platform, commonly deployed on Kafka Connect, emitting row-level change events from databases.

nodes.title: Governed Analytical Data Platform
nodes.summary: Reference architecture for an analytical data platform with layered refinement, embedded quality gates, metadata and lineage, and governance built in.

nodes.title: Batch Extract-Transform-Load
nodes.summary: Periodically extract data sets from sources, transform them and load them into a target, in scheduled batches (ETL or ELT).

nodes.title: Big Bang Data Migration
nodes.summary: Migrate all data in a single cut-over event after rehearsals, switching all users from source to target at once.

nodes.title: Bitemporal Data Model
nodes.summary: Record both valid time and transaction time for each fact so that any past state can be reconstructed as it was true and as it was known.

nodes.title: Change Data Capture
nodes.summary: Detect inserts, updates and deletes in a source database (typically from its transaction log) and propagate them as a change stream to targets.

nodes.title: Concept-to-Model Traceability
nodes.summary: Link every model element at each layer to the governed concept it represents and to the model element it realizes, so meaning and impact can be traced across layers.

nodes.title: Data Contract
nodes.summary: Make the interface between a data producer and its consumers an explicit, versioned, owned agreement covering schema, semantics, quality and service levels, and enforce it automatically.

nodes.title: Data Quality Gate
nodes.summary: Validate data against explicit quality rules at defined points in a data flow and block, quarantine or flag data that fails, with evidence recorded.

nodes.title: Data Virtualization
nodes.summary: Provide an integrated, queryable view over multiple sources at query time without physically copying the data.

nodes.title: Event Sourcing
nodes.summary: Persist every state change as an immutable domain event in an append-only log and derive current and past states by replaying events.

nodes.title: Layered Data Refinement
nodes.summary: Organise an analytical platform in successive layers — raw, conformed, consumption-ready — each with explicit quality, modeling and governance guarantees.

nodes.title: Master Data Hub
nodes.summary: Manage shared master data entities in a hub that performs identity resolution, maintains golden records and cross-references, and distributes master data, in registry, consolidation, coexistence or centralized style.

nodes.title: Metadata Harvesting
nodes.summary: Automatically extract technical, operational and lineage metadata from source systems, pipelines and tools into a central metadata repository on a schedule or event basis.

nodes.title: Phased Data Migration
nodes.summary: Migrate data in successive waves (by product, region or entity), with source and target coexisting and synchronised during the transition.

nodes.title: Reference Data Hub
nodes.summary: Maintain code lists centrally with versions, validity periods and cross-list mappings, and distribute them to consuming systems.

nodes.title: Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2
nodes.summary: In a dimensional model, preserve history of dimension attributes by inserting a new dimension row with its own surrogate key and effective period for each change.

nodes.title: System-Versioned History Table
nodes.summary: Let the database automatically keep every prior version of a row, with system-maintained transaction-time periods, in an associated history table.

nodes.title: Governance as Afterthought
nodes.summary: Governance is applied as a documentation and approval step at the end of delivery, instead of being embedded in the architecture and workflow.

nodes.title: Implicit Semantics
nodes.summary: The meaning of data exists only implicitly in column names, application code or people's heads, instead of in governed definitions.

nodes.title: Migration Without Data Profiling
nodes.summary: Migration mappings are designed from documentation and schema only, without profiling the actual source data.

nodes.title: Overloaded Attribute
nodes.summary: One attribute carries different meanings depending on context, record type or time, instead of separate, well-defined attributes.

nodes.title: Physical-Model-First Design
nodes.summary: Data structures are designed directly as database tables, skipping the conceptual, semantic and information layers.

nodes.title: Point-to-Point Integration Sprawl
nodes.summary: Systems are integrated through many individually built point-to-point interfaces, each with its own mapping, semantics and quality handling.

nodes.title: Declare Epistemic Status on Every Object
nodes.summary: Every knowledge object declares epistemic_status (verified fact, external standard, common practice, expert interpretation, recommendation, hypothesis, experimental) and confidence, and leaves sources empty when no verified source exists.

nodes.title: Separate Lifecycle Status from Knowledge Quality
nodes.summary: Track governance lifecycle (`status`) and knowledge quality (`quality`) as two separate fields, reconcile the spec's Draft/Proposed ambiguity with two initial states, and treat the spec's `approval_status` as derived from `status`.

nodes.title: Store Typed Relationships as Front-Matter Keys
nodes.summary: Represent typed relationships as top-level front-matter keys named after controlled relationship types, each holding a list of wikilinks; store each edge once and derive inverses on export.

nodes.title: Use Markdown and Git as the Initial Knowledge Store
nodes.summary: Implement the knowledge graph initially as Markdown files with YAML front matter in a Git repository, navigable in Obsidian, validated by a script.
nodes.path: 20-architecture-decisions/records/Use Markdown and Git as the Initial Knowledge Store.md

nodes.title: Use Title-Based File Names for Knowledge Objects
nodes.summary: Name each knowledge object file after its title (unique across the repository) and keep the immutable ID in front matter, so Obsidian wikilinks and graph labels are human-readable.
nodes.path: 20-architecture-decisions/records/Use Title-Based File Names for Knowledge Objects.md

nodes.title: Knowledge Base Maturity Model
nodes.summary: Five-level maturity model for an architecture knowledge base, from fragmented to executable, with observable indicators and automatable checks per level.

nodes.title: Data Model Review Checklist
nodes.summary: Checklist for reviewing a data model at its layer, derived from the principles, patterns and anti-patterns in this knowledge base.

nodes.title: Insurance Policy History Example
nodes.summary: Fictitious worked example: taking a history-strategy decision for policy data from requirement to recommendation, using the decision tree, a recommendation rule and a scoring model.

nodes.title: Policy State Is Reproducible As Known At Any Past Date
nodes.summary: Fictitious example requirement: the policy administration must reproduce any policy as it was valid on a date and as it was recorded at another date.
nodes.path: 23-examples/Policy State Is Reproducible As Known At Any Past Date.md

nodes.title: ArchiMate
nodes.summary: ArchiMate — an Open Group modeling language for enterprise architecture covering business, application and technology layers and their relationships.

nodes.title: DAMA-DMBOK
nodes.summary: DAMA Data Management Body of Knowledge — an industry body of knowledge describing data management knowledge areas, including data architecture, modeling, governance, quality and metadata.

nodes.title: GDPR
nodes.summary: General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) — EU regulation on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data.

nodes.title: ISO 8000 Data Quality
nodes.summary: ISO 8000 — a multi-part international standard series on data quality, including data quality management and the exchange of quality master data.

nodes.title: ISO IEC 11179 Metadata Registries
nodes.summary: ISO/IEC 11179 — a multi-part international standard for metadata registries, describing how to register, define, name and identify data elements and related concepts.

nodes.title: ISO IEC 25012 Data Quality Model
nodes.summary: ISO/IEC 25012 — defines a general data quality model for data retained in a structured format within a computer system, with inherent and system-dependent characteristics.

nodes.title: OWL 2
nodes.summary: Web Ontology Language 2 — a W3C language for ontologies with formally defined semantics, enabling reasoning over classes, properties and individuals.

nodes.title: RDF 1.1
nodes.summary: Resource Description Framework 1.1 — the W3C graph data model of subject–predicate–object triples identified by IRIs, underlying SKOS and OWL.

nodes.title: SKOS
nodes.summary: Simple Knowledge Organization System — a W3C data model for representing thesauri, taxonomies, classification schemes and other controlled vocabularies in RDF.

nodes.title: SQL Standard Temporal Support
nodes.summary: Temporal features of the SQL standard (ISO/IEC 9075), introduced in SQL:2011 — application-time period tables and system-versioned tables.

nodes.title: Pattern Realizes a Concept or Principle
nodes.summary: Every pattern realizes at least one concept or principle, keeping solutions traceable to the knowledge they serve.

nodes.title: Technology Implements a Generic Pattern
nodes.summary: Every technology object implements at least one technology-neutral pattern, so technology knowledge never stands on its own.

nodes.title: Architecture Decision Framework
nodes.summary: A structured, machine-readable sequence for taking architecture decisions - question, criteria, conditions, alternatives, consequences, decision, evidence - that links each stage to knowledge objects.

nodes.title: Database History Pattern Decision Tree
nodes.summary: Guides the choice of a history mechanism from explicit reconstruction requirements.

nodes.title: Semantic Modeling Approach Decision Tree
nodes.summary: Guides the choice of semantic model formality — controlled vocabulary, SKOS taxonomy/thesaurus or OWL ontology.

nodes.title: Retroactive Corrections Call for Bitemporal History
nodes.summary: If backdated corrections must be reconstructable and past states must be reproducible, recommend a bitemporal data model.
